tagline: The Asian side's most social waterfront — a beautiful beach club strip, great café scene, and one of Istanbul's most active outdoor communities.

items.name: Mado Caddebostan
items.description: A beloved Istanbul institution with a prime waterfront terrace. Great for ice cream, coffee, and watching the Sea of Marmara.

items.name: Sahil Kahveleri
items.description: A stretch of independent cafés along the Caddebostan waterfront promenade. Relaxed, local, and great for a long afternoon.

items.name: Caddebostan Balık Restoranları
items.description: Several excellent fish restaurants along the waterfront with Princes' Islands views. Great quality at Asian side prices.

items.name: Bağdat Caddesi Restoranları
items.description: The famous Bağdat Avenue (Istanbul's Champs-Élysées) runs through Caddebostan with a wide range of restaurants and cafés at all price points.

items.name: Caddebostan Sahili & Beach Clubs
items.description: A long, well-maintained waterfront with public beaches, beach clubs, and a promenade. The centre of social life on the Asian shore in summer.
items.tip: The beach clubs get packed on summer weekends. Arrive before 10am or go on a weekday for a relaxed experience.

items.name: Bağdat Caddesi Shopping
items.description: A long, tree-lined boulevard packed with fashion boutiques, cafés, and restaurants. The Asian side's answer to İstiklal — more relaxed and less touristy.

tips: Caddebostan is accessible by metro (M4 Göztepe stop, then a short walk or dolmuş to the coast).
Bağdat Caddesi is one of Istanbul's best shopping streets — less touristy and more local than İstiklal.
The beach area is free and open to all. Beach clubs charge entry but include sun loungers and service.
The promenade connects to Suadiye and Fenerbahçe — worth walking the whole stretch.
